title: Teaching himself clarinet
summary: Inspired by a white barber clarinetist, he got a clarinet and learned it note for note without lessons at 16 or 17.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: It was an apple. And, uh, so he told my daddy to give him the brand new one. Because it was hard to work. He was telling me. It was brand new. And he know more about it than I did. And he swapped it for his own. Well, this one was in perfect condition. I was willing because, uh, that one was hard to blow with the brand new ones. So he swapped me. And I never taken a lesson in my life. I just taken the clarinet and sit on the porch in the evening when I come from work or get in the room. And figure out note for note. If I could get make, I could make three notes. Then I'd go look for another note until I learned the whole horn like that. Just note for note, feeling for him until I found him. So I commenced to playing a tune. Anything I could whistle, then I could play it on the clarinet. Well, I played around there for, I'd say about a year and a half.
What age were you then when you started clarinet?

I was around, I was around 17 years old. 16 or 17 years old when I started playing clarinet. And then various bands used to come from here over there. And when they'd come, I'd bring my clarinet. You'd swear I was going to work out. Bring my clarinet. Peter go in. This is big. They have my clarinet with me. I'd get in there and I'd beg them to let me play with them. Sometime they'd turn me down and sometime they'd let me play. But after you let me play once, then they wouldn't have no trouble. I wouldn't have no trouble asking them no more. They'd be begging me to come play then. Well, that's why I used to start playing then.
